newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Debt Office pleased with indexed bond.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Debt Office pleased with indexed bond.

text.p: Swedish National Debt Office chairman Thomas Franzen said on Wednesday he was pleased with the success of the debt office's index-linked bond but expected to reduce the issue volume in the future.
"We've had a net issue volume of over 40 billion crowns this year, so we can say we have established this instrument," Franzen told Reuters.
"We'll be reducing the offered indexed bond volume via our on-tap sales," he said, adding this would apply mainly to shorter maturities.
Short index-linked bonds offered very attractive interest rates to investors, Franzen said.
"If you look at the very shortest durations, the real interest rate is such that you pay nothing to get rid of (the risk of) inflation," he said.
The fact the real interest rates were so high is because of the fall in nominal rates. Real market rates had not kept up, he said.
"Real interest rates should begin to move downwards," Franzen said.
